correctness.rationale: For each n>=6 the proposed middle-even witness tuples were checked symbolically: if a in [6,2n-4] is even, (1,2,a-2,a-1) for a<=n+1 or (a-n,n,a-n+1,n-1) for a>=n+2 is positive, strictly distinct and has precisely the required six allowed sums. Without middle evens E is one of four triples in {2,4,2n-2,2n}; the two explicit boundary tuples eliminate three triples. The surviving {2,2n-2,2n} admits no witness: three same-parity summands force three distinct even sums among only the two even values >=4, while a two/two split forces two opposite-parity larger summands at least n, whose sum exceeds 2n. An independently written brute-force enumerator reproduced exactly the surviving triple for each n=6,...,12, corroborative rather than an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Finite checks only corroborate the identified closed proof steps and do not constitute infinite verification.
